\textnormal{Unique factorization therefore permits a product over primes. For each prime ell, its local power series is geometric.}

statement: \textnormal{Let }\Omega(n)\textnormal{ be the total number of prime factors of the positive integer }n\textnormal{ counted with multiplicity, with }\Omega(1)=0.\textnormal{ Define the zeta function by its convergent series.}\quad\Omega(12)=3,\qquad\zeta(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}n^{-s}\ (s>1).\quad\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{\Omega(n)}}{n^{9}}=?

analyticCertificate: Finite prime products sum precisely over integers supported on those primes. Absolute convergence lets the finite support restriction grow to all integers. The zeta Euler product follows by the same positive geometric expansion; dividing the two convergent products is legitimate because zeta(s)>0 for real s>1.
